pathway.title: Energy Transfer LP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has eased through earnings, not repayment. Total debt was USD 68,850 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 68,333 million at December 31, 2025, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 19,216 million from USD 15,984 million, which moves total debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 4.28x to 3.58x and net debt from 4.20x to 3.53x [financial base: leverage and coverage]. Nine months of 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 15,034 million compares with USD 11,802 million, and the Sunoco LP segment supplied USD 560 million of the USD 1,193 million Q3 increase [financial base: reported results; business context: operating model]. The issuer's covenant leverage ratio under the Five-Year Credit Facility was 2.83x against a maximum of 5.00x (5.50x in a Specified Acquisition Period), so on the issuer's own basis headroom is 2.17 turns, which would allow Adjusted EBITDA to fall by about 43.4 percent at constant debt (Calculations C1) [financial base: leverage and coverage]. The covenant definition is not supplied and gives a lower ratio than the simple one, so the headroom is indicative only.

Earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA is an issuer non-GAAP measure that for nine months 2026 adds back USD 519 million of unrealized commodity losses, removes USD 445 million of inventory valuation gains and includes USD 588 million of Adjusted EBITDA of unconsolidated affiliates [financial base: reconciliation]. On operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization, total debt is 3.90x LTM against 4.65x for FY2025, so the improving direction survives a GAAP cross-check, but the level is higher than the covenant figure. Revenue of USD 124,528 million LTM is mostly pass-through product sales (fees were 14.5 percent of FY2025 revenue), so margin analysis must use Adjusted EBITDA [business context: operating model].

Cash flow covers interest but not distributions plus growth capital. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid 5.43x LTM and interest expense 5.14x; interest expense takes 19.4 percent of LTM Adjusted EBITDA (Calculations C2) [financial base: leverage and coverage]. LTM operating cash flow of USD 13,569 million less capital expenditure of USD 7,487 million leaves free cash flow of USD 6,082 million, below distributions of USD 6,955 million to partners and noncontrolling interests, a shortfall of USD 873 million that arose in the fourth quarter of 2025 [financial base: cash flow quality]. On the issuer's own Distributable Cash Flow basis, which excludes growth capital, the partnership is close to self-funding: for nine months 2026, Distributable Cash Flow attributable to partners, as adjusted, of USD 7,813 million covered distributions of USD 3,515 million 2.22x and left USD 4,298 million against accrual-basis growth capital of USD 4,432 million, a gap of USD 134 million (Calculations C3; Q3 release page:8, Q3 10-Q page:86). Growth capital is guided at USD 5.4 billion to USD 5.6 billion for 2026 and about USD 7 billion for 2027 [business context: operating model], so the partnership will keep relying on debt and subsidiary-level capital.

Liquidity is ample in aggregate and thinner at the parent. Cash of USD 926 million plus undrawn facilities of USD 7,766 million gives USD 8,692 million, but only USD 4,406 million is the parent's Five-Year Credit Facility; USD 2,300 million belongs to Sunoco LP and USD 1,060 million to USAC, and cash is consolidated [financial base: liquidity]. The parent commitment steps down by USD 160 million on April 11, 2027.

The near-term maturity wall is smaller at the parent than CP-1 implied. The issuer states that about USD 4,350 million of principal due on or before September 30, 2027 is classed as long-term on refinancing intent and ability (Q3 10-Q page:88). Adding the instruments in the December 31, 2025 table that mature by that date and were not redeemed in 2026 gives USD 3,300 million at the parent (6.05% notes of USD 1,000 million due December 1, 2026; 4.40% notes of USD 700 million; 4.20% notes of USD 600 million; and two 5.50% notes due June 1, 2027 of USD 44 million and USD 956 million) and USD 1,050 million at Sunoco LP (5.625% and 5.875% notes due 2027, 550, 499 and 1), which sums to USD 4,350 million (Calculations C4; 10-K page:322). This is an Analyst Interpretation: the footnote does not split the amount and the 2027 months for the Sunoco LP notes are not printed. It corrects the CP-1 sentence that compared the whole USD 4,350 million with the parent's USD 4,406 million of availability: that comparison overstates the parent's need, though the parent still has USD 3,300 million to refinance within about eleven months, including USD 1,000 million on December 1, 2026, which is within a month of the as-of date.

Structure matters for the parent's creditors. The parent's notes and debentures plus Five-Year Credit Facility are USD 52,035 million of principal and its senior notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries; Sunoco LP and USAC together carry USD 16,276 million with separate facilities [financial base: debt and capital structure; business context: ownership and capital allocation]. As an indicative proxy, parent principal over LTM Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Sunoco LP and USAC segments (USD 14,946 million) is 3.48x (Calculations C5). That proxy ignores the cash distributions the parent receives from them (Sunoco LP USD 306 million and USAC USD 73 million for nine months 2026 on the Distributable Cash Flow basis, Q3 release page:7) and counts non-wholly-owned joint ventures at 100 percent, so it shows only that excluding the subsidiaries does not make parent leverage lower than the consolidated figure of 3.58x by much. Whether parent-level coverage is adequate cannot be tested without parent-only statements, which are not supplied.

Hybrids and preferred equity shifted toward debt. The parent's junior subordinated notes are USD 5,550 million of principal after the July 2026 issues of USD 1,750 million (on CP-1's calculation), the Series H preferred units of USD 900 million were redeemed, and preferred equity outstanding is USD 2,480 million [financial base: debt and capital structure; business context: transaction summary]. Equity credit for these instruments is Not supplied.

Acquisitions and control are the main forward risks. Vaquero (total consideration about USD 2.63 billion, USD 1.95 billion in cash) is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and Offen (about USD 600 million) closed on October 27, 2026 at Sunoco LP; the cash consideration for Vaquero equals 44.3 percent of the parent's revolver availability, and the funding plan is Not supplied [business context: transaction summary]. One individual holds 81.2 percent of the general partner and all Class A units, so creditors have no governance rights and depend on covenants; derivative suits are pending [business context: ownership and governance]. The issuer's state of organisation and exchange changed in 2026 and the filing explaining it is not supplied [source readiness; business context: conflicts]. Contingent matters are moderate against EBITDA: accruals of USD 536 million, additional reasonably possible losses up to approximately USD 76 million, and unrecorded favourable verdicts of approximately USD 795 million in aggregate, of which USD 393 million was recorded in October 2026 [business context: operating model and timeline].

cells.text: "The primary activities in which we are engaged, which are located in the United States, are as follows: •natural gas operations, including the following: ◦natural gas midstream and intrastate transportation and storage; ◦interstate natural gas transportation and storage; and •crude oil, NGL and refined products transportation, terminalling services and acquisition and marketing activities"
Multi-commodity network; earnings depend on volumes, capacity reservation and marketing margins rather than one product

Approximately 12,200 miles of intrastate pipelines with approximately 24 Bcf/d of capacity; customers pay "a demand fee, which is a fixed fee for the reservation of an agreed amount of capacity" plus transportation fees and fuel retention
Demand fees give contracted revenue visibility; volume-based fees and gas sales add exposure to throughput and spreads
Approximately 20,090 miles of interstate pipelines with approximately 20.1 Bcf/d of capacity, plus about 7,080 miles through joint ventures; rates regulated by the FERC
Regulated cost-of-service and negotiated rates stabilise cash flow but face rate-case risk; Panhandle's rate proceedings are on appeal (Q3 10-Q page:60)

Import and regasification terminal with all revenue from "long-term contracts with a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Dutch Shell plc"; liquefaction development suspended in December 2025 and several offtake agreements terminated
Regasification income depends on one counterparty; suspension avoids a large capital commitment, a point for capital discipline

Gathering, treating and processing with aggregate processing capacity of approximately 13.5 Bcf/d; results "derived primarily from margins we earn from natural gas volumes that are gathered, transported, purchased and sold"
Margin exposure to volumes and NGL and gas prices; producer drilling activity is a driver

About 5,750 miles of NGL pipelines, Mont Belvieu fractionation of 1.15 MMBbls/d, working NGL storage of about 63 MMBbls; revenue "principally generated from fees charged to customers under dedicated contracts or take-or-pay contracts"
Fee-based contracts with minimum commitments support cash conversion; the segment was the largest contributor to Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (Calculations C2)

More than 18,000 miles of crude trunk and gathering pipelines, equity stakes in seven pipeline systems and about 73 MMBbls of terminal storage; tariffs filed with the FERC and state regulators, plus acquisition and marketing
Tariff income is stable; marketing margin is commodity-spread dependent; Bakken Pipeline carries separate project debt
Sunoco LP distributes "over 15 billion gallons annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner branded locations"; acquired Parkland on October 31, 2025 with operations in 26 countries
High-revenue, thin-margin distribution; revenue and margin are exposed to fuel prices, foreign exchange (Canadian dollar functional currency for Parkland) and refinery risk
USAC provides compression services in unconventional plays, "primarily in connection with infrastructure applications"
Contracted fee income linked to gathering activity; separate credit facility and notes

Gathering, transportation and other fees were 14.5 percent of FY2025 total revenues and 10.0 percent for nine months 2026 (Calculations C1); the rest is product sales including refined products, crude, NGL and natural gas
Revenue is mostly pass-through product sales, so revenue growth overstates earnings growth; margin analysis must use Adjusted EBITDA (CP-1)
"During the year ended December 31, 2025, none of our customers individually accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated revenues."
Low single-customer concentration at the consolidated level; segment- or contract-level concentration is Not supplied

FY2025 cost of products sold 63,495, operating expenses 5,867, selling, general and administrative 1,180 against revenues of 85,536
Cost of products sold is 74.2 percent of revenue (C3), so margin depends on spreads, with fixed operating cost a smaller part

Expected 2026 capital expenditure of 5,250 growth and 1,150 maintenance excluding Sunoco LP and USAC, per the 10-K; later guidance of "$5.4 billion to $5.6 billion in growth capital for 2026 and approximately $7 billion for 2027"

Hugh Brinson Pipeline Phase I placed in full service September 1, 2026 and Phase II due in the first quarter of 2027; Mustang Draw II plant in service in October; Bear II plant planned for the third quarter of 2027; South Mississippi Pipeline FID at about 1.6 billion US$ with Energy Transfer "likely" a 51 percent owner; Frac X planned for the first half of 2029

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Scale and diversity: eight segments, no customer above 10 percent of revenue and a largest segment of 24.3 percent of Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, which limits single-asset or single-customer risk (Documentary Fact; business context). (2) Earnings momentum and conversion: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 19,216 million, raised 2026 guidance of USD 19.7 billion to USD 19.9 billion, and Distributable Cash Flow covering distributions 2.22x for nine months (Documentary Fact for the figures; guidance is Management Language). (3) Liquidity: USD 8,692 million including subsidiary facilities, USD 4,406 million at the parent, and revolver extended to 2029 (Documentary Fact; financial base). (4) Demonstrated market access: USD 3,000 million of senior notes in January 2026 and USD 1,750 million of junior subordinated notes in July 2026, with USD 4,350 million of near-term maturities classed as refinanceable (Documentary Fact). (5) Covenant headroom on the issuer's reported basis of 2.17 turns (Documentary Fact for the figures; the headroom is an Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. (1) Free cash flow does not cover distributions: USD 873 million LTM shortfall, with growth capital of about USD 7 billion guided for 2027 (Documentary Fact; guidance is Management Language; the funding implication is an Analyst Interpretation). (2) Leverage fell through earnings growth concentrated in the Sunoco LP segment, whose creditors rank ahead of the parent in subsidiary assets (Documentary Fact; the priority statement is an Analyst Interpretation). (3) Debt-funded acquisitions continue with Vaquero and Offen, funding not stated, so pro forma leverage is Not calculable (Insufficient Information). (4) Control by an individual through the general partner, limited unitholder rights and pending derivative litigation (Documentary Fact). (5) Unresolved identity change and missing executed documents, so obligor, covenant and guarantee analysis rests on filing summaries (Insufficient Information). (6) Adjusted EBITDA dependence: add-backs and affiliates' EBITDA, and a covenant ratio on a definition not supplied (Documentary Fact; dependence is Analyst Interpretation).

runs.text: Pending and recent transactions, with status. Vaquero: on October 6, 2026 Energy Transfer entered a definitive agreement to acquire all equity interests of Vaquero and related assets "for total consideration of approximately $2.63 billion", consisting of $1.95 billion in cash and approximately 33.3 million newly issued Energy Transfer common units; it owns natural gas gathering, processing and transportation assets in the Delaware Basin and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals (Q3 10-Q page:9 and page:57). The release describes it as a "bolt-on transaction for approximately $2.6 billion" (Q3 release page:2). The source of the cash is not stated, so the effect on the parent's liquidity and debt is Not supplied. For scale only, the cash is 44.3 percent of the parent revolver availability of 4,406 US$m at September 30, 2026 in CP-1 (C5); no funding plan is implied.

Subsidiary transactions: Sunoco LP completed the Offen acquisition for approximately 600 US$m in cash on October 27, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:58), which is a subsequent event after the September 30 balance sheet; Sunoco LP also completed TanQuid on January 16, 2026 for 206 million euros (239 US$m) with assumed debt of 346 US$m fair value, and Delta on April 1, 2026 for about 81 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:57). USAC completed J-W Power on January 12, 2026 for about 912 US$m, of which about 455 US$m was cash and about 457 US$m was 18.2 million new USAC common units (Q3 10-Q page:58). TanQuid was funded using Sunoco LP cash on hand and its credit facility (Q3 10-Q page:57); these subsidiary transactions consolidate into Energy Transfer's debt.

New debt issues and redemptions in 2025 and 2026, from the 10-K and Q3 10-Q. Energy Transfer parent: March 2025, 650 US$m of 5.20% senior notes due 2030, 1.25 billion US$ of 5.70% notes due 2035 and 1.10 billion US$ of 6.20% notes due 2055, with proceeds to refinance debt; August 2025, 1.20 billion US$ of Series 2025A and 800 US$m of Series 2025B junior subordinated notes due 2056; January 2026, 1.00 billion US$ each of 4.55% notes due 2031, 5.35% notes due 2036 and 6.30% notes due 2056; July 2026, 650 US$m of Series 2026A and 1.10 billion US$ of Series 2026B junior subordinated notes due 2057 (together 1,750 US$m), initially at 6.550% and 6.700%, with proceeds to redeem the Series H preferred units, repay Five-Year Credit Facility borrowings and for general partnership purposes (10-K page:325; Q3 10-Q page:17). Redemptions: 4.05% notes of 1.00 billion US$ (March 2025), 2.90% notes of 1.00 billion US$ (May 2025), 5.95% notes of 400 US$m (September 2025), 4.75% notes of 1.00 billion US$ (January 2026), 5.625% notes of 600 US$m (February 2026) and 3.90% notes of 550 US$m (July 2026). Sunoco LP: March 2025, 1.00 billion US$ of 6.25% notes due 2033; September 2025, 1.00 billion US$ of 5.625% notes due 2031 and 900 US$m of 5.875% notes due 2034 to fund Parkland; March 2026, 600 US$m each of 5.375% notes due 2031 and 5.625% notes due 2034, used partly to redeem 500 US$m and 600 US$m of 6.000% notes; Parkland note exchanges in November 2025. USAC: September 2025, 750 US$m of 6.250% notes due 2033; September 2026, 600 US$m of 6.750% notes due 2035.

Preferred and hybrid: the Series H preferred units of 900 US$m were redeemed on August 17, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:19 and page:21); the Series F redemption of 500 US$m occurred in 2025 (10-K page:289; Q3 10-Q page:87). The creditor mechanics are in the CP-1 handoff: the parent's junior subordinated notes are 5,550 US$m in principal on CP-1's calculation, and the preferred equity outstanding fell to 2,480 US$m.

Status labels: Vaquero is agreed and unclosed; Offen is completed after quarter end; the October 8, 2026 termination of Sunoco LP's NuStar receivables financing agreement is completed (Q3 10-Q page:18); the change of state and exchange is documented only on cover pages. fields.value: Energy Transfer LP is a large, diversified midstream operator whose eight reportable segments cover natural gas gathering, processing and transportation, NGL and refined products, crude oil, and two publicly traded consolidated subsidiaries: Sunoco LP (fuel distribution and terminals) and USAC (compression). The 10-K states that no customer individually accounted for more than 10 percent of revenue in FY2025, and in Q3 2026 no segment contributed more than a quarter of Adjusted EBITDA on the figures in CP-1, so concentration risk by customer or segment is limited on the documents read. The creditor-relevant features are three. First, change: Sunoco LP acquired Parkland on October 31, 2025, which enlarged that segment's revenue and earnings (it supplied 560 US$m of the 1,193 US$m increase in Q3 Adjusted EBITDA in CP-1) and added subsidiary debt, so the reported leverage improvement depends on a subsidiary with separate creditors. Second, a continuing programme of acquisitions and growth capital: J-W Power, TanQuid, Delta and Offen in 2026, Vaquero agreed on October 6, 2026 for about 2.63 billion US$ (1.95 billion US$ cash plus about 33.3 million new common units), growth capital guided at 5.4 billion to 5.6 billion US$ for 2026 and about 7 billion US$ for 2027. Third, structure and control: the parent's senior notes are unguaranteed by subsidiaries, a single individual controls the general partner, and the issuer's state of organisation and exchange changed in 2026 without a supplied explanation.

fields.value: Behaviour category (issuer level, documented actions only): Neutral or Mixed. Distributions are paid from available cash and increased while growth capital is large, and growing distributions coexist with a falling reported covenant leverage ratio (CP-1) and debt-funded growth. No priming, uptier, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release was found in the pages read. Evidence quality: High for the filings; the scoring dimensions informed are control concentration, distribution policy and capital allocation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation mechanics. Cash acquisitions at the parent and at Sunoco LP and USAC are funded by cash, commercial paper and facility borrowings or new notes, raising consolidated debt unless offset by EBITDA; unit consideration reduces cash needs but increases distributions. Paying 100 percent of available cash leaves growth to be financed by debt and subsidiary-level capital, as CP-1 shows a negative LTM free cash flow after distributions of 873 US$m. Preferred redemption funded by junior subordinated notes raises debt-ranking claims while lowering the preferred coupon base (the notes' initial rates are 6.550% and 6.700%, against 6.500% on Series H, 10-K page:336); this is an Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: no customer above 10 percent of revenue (10-K page:39); demand-fee and take-or-pay contracts (10-K page:8 and page:11). Mechanic: contracted fee streams cover a share of margin, while marketing, processing margins and fuel distribution vary with commodity spreads. Implication: earnings are more stable than the product-sales revenue suggests, but the proportion of margin that is contracted is Not supplied, so the coverage of fixed charges by contracted income cannot be stated. Counter-evidence: working capital and unrealized commodity swings in cash flow (CP-1).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Subsidiary leverage and structural subordination. Evidence: separate Sunoco LP and USAC facilities and notes, and parent notes unguaranteed (10-K page:325; Q3 10-Q page:18). Mechanic: subsidiary creditors rank ahead of the parent in subsidiary assets and cash, while Sunoco LP supplied 560 US$m of the Q3 Adjusted EBITDA increase (CP-1). Implication: the parent's creditors benefit from growth in those subsidiaries only through distributions, so parent leverage measured on consolidated EBITDA overstates parent-available coverage; this is a consideration for CP-2, not a conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Acquisition-led growth and funding. Evidence: Vaquero, Offen, J-W Power, TanQuid and Parkland (Q3 10-Q page:57 and page:58; 10-K page:313). Mechanic: cash components add to borrowings or draw on facilities; unit components dilute distributions per unit. Implication: leverage tolerance depends on EBITDA growth outpacing debt; the Vaquero funding plan is Not supplied, so pro forma leverage is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Control and governance. Evidence: 81.2 percent of the general partner and all Class A units (10-K page:132); derivative litigation (Q3 10-Q page:32). Mechanic: unitholders cannot remove the general partner without the vote described, and creditors have no governance rights. Implication: monitoring posture should rest on covenants and disclosure; the partnership agreement is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Identity and listing change. Evidence: cover pages and 8-K12B reference. Mechanic: a change of state of organisation could alter the obligor, the governing documents or successor language. Implication: structural analysis should wait for the filing; the conflict logged below counters any assumption of continuity.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Energy Transfer LP as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 and prior period FY2025, in USD. It draws on the three upstream handoffs (source readiness, financial base, business and transaction context) and re-checks a few filing pages where a conclusion needed them. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Run context (settings, not issuer evidence): context sha256 dfad783f6af55323b89ba2b387376722ec78e773820c07687193a91e09314cf8.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Direct checks beyond the handoffs, each cited where used: 10-K page:322 (instrument table for the near-term maturities), Q3 10-Q page:86 and page:88 (growth capital and the footnote on borrowings classified as long-term), Q3 release page:8 (Distributable Cash Flow and distributions), Q3 release page:7.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Energy Transfer's debt looks serviceable on current earnings and liquidity, but it depends on subsidiary earnings growth and continued market access. The strongest support is scale and diversity: USD 19,216 million of LTM Adjusted EBITDA across eight segments, no customer above 10 percent of revenue, and USD 8,692 million of cash and undrawn facilities. The weakest point is that free cash flow does not cover distributions and growth capital, so leverage of 3.58x (4.28x for FY2025) rests on earnings growth, much of it from Sunoco LP, and on refinancing about USD 4,350 million due by September 30, 2027. Covenant terms, the 2026 change of state and the Vaquero funding plan decide whether the view holds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has eased through earnings, not repayment. Total debt was USD 68,850 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 68,333 million at December 31, 2025, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 19,216 million from USD 15,984 million, which moves total debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 4.28x to 3.58x and net debt from 4.20x to 3.53x [financial base: leverage and coverage]. Nine months of 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 15,034 million compares with USD 11,802 million, and the Sunoco LP segment supplied USD 560 million of the USD 1,193 million Q3 increase [financial base: reported results; business context: operating model]. The issuer's covenant leverage ratio under the Five-Year Credit Facility was 2.83x against a maximum of 5.00x (5.50x in a Specified Acquisition Period), so on the issuer's own basis headroom is 2.17 turns, which would allow Adjusted EBITDA to fall by about 43.4 percent at constant debt (Calculations C1) [financial base: leverage and coverage]. The covenant definition is not supplied and gives a lower ratio than the simple one, so the headroom is indicative only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA is an issuer non-GAAP measure that for nine months 2026 adds back USD 519 million of unrealized commodity losses, removes USD 445 million of inventory valuation gains and includes USD 588 million of Adjusted EBITDA of unconsolidated affiliates [financial base: reconciliation]. On operating income plus depreciation, depletion and amortization, total debt is 3.90x LTM against 4.65x for FY2025, so the improving direction survives a GAAP cross-check, but the level is higher than the covenant figure. Revenue of USD 124,528 million LTM is mostly pass-through product sales (fees were 14.5 percent of FY2025 revenue), so margin analysis must use Adjusted EBITDA [business context: operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow covers interest but not distributions plus growth capital. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid 5.43x LTM and interest expense 5.14x; interest expense takes 19.4 percent of LTM Adjusted EBITDA (Calculations C2) [financial base: leverage and coverage]. LTM operating cash flow of USD 13,569 million less capital expenditure of USD 7,487 million leaves free cash flow of USD 6,082 million, below distributions of USD 6,955 million to partners and noncontrolling interests, a shortfall of USD 873 million that arose in the fourth quarter of 2025 [financial base: cash flow quality]. On the issuer's own Distributable Cash Flow basis, which excludes growth capital, the partnership is close to self-funding: for nine months 2026, Distributable Cash Flow attributable to partners, as adjusted, of USD 7,813 million covered distributions of USD 3,515 million 2.22x and left USD 4,298 million against accrual-basis growth capital of USD 4,432 million, a gap of USD 134 million (Calculations C3; Q3 release page:8, Q3 10-Q page:86). Growth capital is guided at USD 5.4 billion to USD 5.6 billion for 2026 and about USD 7 billion for 2027 [business context: operating model], so the partnership will keep relying on debt and subsidiary-level capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample in aggregate and thinner at the parent. Cash of USD 926 million plus undrawn facilities of USD 7,766 million gives USD 8,692 million, but only USD 4,406 million is the parent's Five-Year Credit Facility; USD 2,300 million belongs to Sunoco LP and USD 1,060 million to USAC, and cash is consolidated [financial base: liquidity]. The parent commitment steps down by USD 160 million on April 11, 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The near-term maturity wall is smaller at the parent than CP-1 implied. The issuer states that about USD 4,350 million of principal due on or before September 30, 2027 is classed as long-term on refinancing intent and ability (Q3 10-Q page:88). Adding the instruments in the December 31, 2025 table that mature by that date and were not redeemed in 2026 gives USD 3,300 million at the parent (6.05% notes of USD 1,000 million due December 1, 2026; 4.40% notes of USD 700 million; 4.20% notes of USD 600 million; and two 5.50% notes due June 1, 2027 of USD 44 million and USD 956 million) and USD 1,050 million at Sunoco LP (5.625% and 5.875% notes due 2027, 550, 499 and 1), which sums to USD 4,350 million (Calculations C4; 10-K page:322). This is an Analyst Interpretation: the footnote does not split the amount and the 2027 months for the Sunoco LP notes are not printed. It corrects the CP-1 sentence that compared the whole USD 4,350 million with the parent's USD 4,406 million of availability: that comparison overstates the parent's need, though the parent still has USD 3,300 million to refinance within about eleven months, including USD 1,000 million on December 1, 2026, which is within a month of the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure matters for the parent's creditors. The parent's notes and debentures plus Five-Year Credit Facility are USD 52,035 million of principal and its senior notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries; Sunoco LP and USAC together carry USD 16,276 million with separate facilities [financial base: debt and capital structure; business context: ownership and capital allocation]. As an indicative proxy, parent principal over LTM Adjusted EBITDA excluding the Sunoco LP and USAC segments (USD 14,946 million) is 3.48x (Calculations C5). That proxy ignores the cash distributions the parent receives from them (Sunoco LP USD 306 million and USAC USD 73 million for nine months 2026 on the Distributable Cash Flow basis, Q3 release page:7) and counts non-wholly-owned joint ventures at 100 percent, so it shows only that excluding the subsidiaries does not make parent leverage lower than the consolidated figure of 3.58x by much. Whether parent-level coverage is adequate cannot be tested without parent-only statements, which are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hybrids and preferred equity shifted toward debt. The parent's junior subordinated notes are USD 5,550 million of principal after the July 2026 issues of USD 1,750 million (on CP-1's calculation), the Series H preferred units of USD 900 million were redeemed, and preferred equity outstanding is USD 2,480 million [financial base: debt and capital structure; business context: transaction summary]. Equity credit for these instruments is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions and control are the main forward risks. Vaquero (total consideration about USD 2.63 billion, USD 1.95 billion in cash) is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and Offen (about USD 600 million) closed on October 27, 2026 at Sunoco LP; the cash consideration for Vaquero equals 44.3 percent of the parent's revolver availability, and the funding plan is Not supplied [business context: transaction summary]. One individual holds 81.2 percent of the general partner and all Class A units, so creditors have no governance rights and depend on covenants; derivative suits are pending [business context: ownership and governance]. The issuer's state of organisation and exchange changed in 2026 and the filing explaining it is not supplied [source readiness; business context: conflicts]. Contingent matters are moderate against EBITDA: accruals of USD 536 million, additional reasonably possible losses up to approximately USD 76 million, and unrecorded favourable verdicts of approximately USD 795 million in aggregate, of which USD 393 million was recorded in October 2026 [business context: operating model and timeline].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Scale and diversity: eight segments, no customer above 10 percent of revenue and a largest segment of 24.3 percent of Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, which limits single-asset or single-customer risk (Documentary Fact; business context). (2) Earnings momentum and conversion: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 19,216 million, raised 2026 guidance of USD 19.7 billion to USD 19.9 billion, and Distributable Cash Flow covering distributions 2.22x for nine months (Documentary Fact for the figures; guidance is Management Language). (3) Liquidity: USD 8,692 million including subsidiary facilities, USD 4,406 million at the parent, and revolver extended to 2029 (Documentary Fact; financial base). (4) Demonstrated market access: USD 3,000 million of senior notes in January 2026 and USD 1,750 million of junior subordinated notes in July 2026, with USD 4,350 million of near-term maturities classed as refinanceable (Documentary Fact). (5) Covenant headroom on the issuer's reported basis of 2.17 turns (Documentary Fact for the figures; the headroom is an Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Free cash flow does not cover distributions: USD 873 million LTM shortfall, with growth capital of about USD 7 billion guided for 2027 (Documentary Fact; guidance is Management Language; the funding implication is an Analyst Interpretation). (2) Leverage fell through earnings growth concentrated in the Sunoco LP segment, whose creditors rank ahead of the parent in subsidiary assets (Documentary Fact; the priority statement is an Analyst Interpretation). (3) Debt-funded acquisitions continue with Vaquero and Offen, funding not stated, so pro forma leverage is Not calculable (Insufficient Information). (4) Control by an individual through the general partner, limited unitholder rights and pending derivative litigation (Documentary Fact). (5) Unresolved identity change and missing executed documents, so obligor, covenant and guarantee analysis rests on filing summaries (Insufficient Information). (6) Adjusted EBITDA dependence: add-backs and affiliates' EBITDA, and a covenant ratio on a definition not supplied (Documentary Fact; dependence is Analyst Interpretation).

The footnote covers parent and Sunoco LP notes; the parent portion is about USD 3,300 million (Calculations C4). CP-1 was not edited; this answer supersedes that sentence.
